counterexample: The diamond lattice M3 = {0, a, b, c, 1} with a, b, c pairwise incomparable: it is a finite (hence complete) lattice, so it is an object of CLat, but a AND (b OR c) = a AND 1 = a while (a AND b) OR (a AND c) = 0 OR 0 = 0, so it violates even finite distributivity and therefore the frame distributivity law. Hence M3 is an object of CLat that is not an object of Frm, so ob(CLat) is not a subcollection of ob(Frm).
reasoning_summary: Step 0001-0002 cites 'Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism' to conclude that CLat consists of a subcollection of the objects AND a subcollection of the morphisms of Frm. The cited result concerns only morphisms (and presupposes that its source and target are frames); it says nothing about the object collections. The object inclusion required by the definition of subcategory (ob(D) contained in ob(C)) is in fact false: a frame is by definition a complete lattice satisfying the infinite distributive law, whereas an arbitrary complete lattice need not be distributive at all (e.g. M3). So step 0002 is both unjustified by its citation and false as stated, which also undermines the concluding step 0009. Steps 0004-0007 (composition is composition of mappings, identities are identity mappings) are unobjectionable, but they cannot repair the failed object-inclusion condition. Stopped at step 0002.
